# --- Respawn: L4D2 VENDORED WORKSHOP VPKs --------------------------------------
# THE WORKSHOP HAS NO VERSION CONCEPT. `ws:3022416274 latest` is not a pin, it is a
# promise that whatever the author published most recently is what you get — and an
# author can republish under the same id with no signal at all.
#
# That collides badly with this repo's image tags, which are content hashes over the
# COPYed files (see CLAUDE.md). An upstream republish either silently moves the tag,
# forcing a rebuild nobody asked for, or — worse — does not, because the fetch happened
# outside the build context. Either way "the same tag" stops meaning the same server.
#
# So a Workshop VPK is SNAPSHOTTED: downloaded once, hashed, and vendored to the private
# state bucket. This file is the pin. The hash is checked on every fetch, and a mismatch
# is a hard failure rather than a warning — a VPK that is not the one this manifest names
# is exactly the thing being guarded against.
#
# THE S3 KEY CARRIES THE HASH, so re-snapshotting writes a NEW object beside the old one
# instead of overwriting it. An older commit of this repo keeps fetching the bytes it was
# built and tested against, which is the whole point of pinning and is lost the moment
# the key is just `<id>.vpk`.
#
# Re-pinning is a deliberate act: `scripts/snapshot-workshop.sh` rewrites the hashes and
# `scripts/publish-vendor.sh` uploads them. The resulting diff IS the review.
#
# Use the PRIVATE state bucket (respawn-state-*), never the public FastDL one. These are
# somebody else's copyrighted work; mirroring them world-readable is a different act from
# keeping a build reproducible.
#
# Format:  <workshop-id>  <sha256>  <bytes>  <captured>  # name
#
# `captured` is the date the bytes were taken, NOT an upstream version — the Workshop
# does not expose one. It says how stale the snapshot is and nothing more.

2634208272  26b4169dc12422c1374e9fae8bbddd8f973f9307be71912011600a03f9ce6ad8    201405  2026-08-30  # Left 4 Lib — MANDATORY, L4B does nothing without it
